findings.summary: The span correction landed in the backlog only; ADR-0043 -- edited by this same diff -- still states `[0, max(byteStart + byteLen))` as correct, and so does backlog.md:60.
findings.detail: Criterion 5 (backlog.md:64) now says the `[0, max(byteStart+byteLen))` span is UNREADABLE and I verified that: SegmentReader.open checks the footer magic at format/src/main/java/binjava/format/SegmentReader.java:71 before the directory loop, so a prefix cut at the last wanted run throws "segment is truncated: no footer magic", and ConsumerClient.decodeInto (client/src/main/java/binjava/client/ConsumerClient.java:78) calls open on the whole array with no partial path. But the diff amends ADR-0043 only with a Status note at :167 about OWNERSHIP. Line 62 of that same file still reads: "SO THE ONE REQUEST SPANS `[0, max(byteStart + byteLen))` ... That is still one request, it leaves every run decodable". backlog.md:60 (M5.44's done cell) repeats it verbatim -- "The single request spans `[0, max(byteStart+byteLen))`, header included ... still ONE request, and the run stays decodable. ADR-0043 corrects it" -- and is unchanged here.
findings.failure_scenario: A taker of M5.45c reads ADR-0043, the normative record for this decision, and implements the ranged GET decision (b) prescribes: `Range: bytes=0-(max(byteStart+byteLen)-1)`. Every `direct` delivery then throws IOException "segment is truncated: no footer magic" out of SegmentReader.open:71 before one record decodes, and the counting fetcher asserting one request per (node, segment) stays green because it counts requests and not decodes -- exactly the failure criterion 5 was rewritten to prevent. The correction is one clause in three places and landed in one; this is the restated-prose pattern the M5.44 cell itself records paying for.

findings.summary: New criterion 1d demands `read-only` be "asserted ON THE ASSEMBLED PATH and not only in GrantIssuerTest" -- read-only is asserted nowhere, and no type in the path represents it.
findings.detail: GrantIssuerTest's sections are criterion 1 (startup refusal, :103), criterion 2 (the TTL ceiling, :178) and criterion 3 (one key, :277). There is no read-only assertion in it, none in PresignConformance, and nothing in `SignedUrl`, `Grant` or `BinStore.presign` carries a verb or a permission a test could read -- `presign(String key, Duration ttl)` has no method parameter, so a stand-in cannot even express a WRITE grant to be refused. M5.37's own cell already names this as the half that is "mechanically uncheckable from outside" and leaves it resting on `BinStore.presign`'s javadoc at rung 7. The ONE KEY half of 1d is genuinely assertable on the assembled path; the read-only half is not.
findings.failure_scenario: The taker of M5.45d writes `assertThat(grant.url()).doesNotContain("PUT")` (or similar) against `StoreFakes.CanPresign`'s synthesised URL. It passes for every implementation, including one that signs a write grant, because the only thing observable is a string the fixture itself minted -- the same tautology M5.37 measured and deleted from PresignConformance ("its first two assertions were TAUTOLOGIES restating SignedUrl's constructor"). The criterion reads discharged while constraining nothing. The honest form is: ONE KEY asserted on the assembled path; read-only stated as resting on presign's contract with M9's real backend owning the check, which is what M5.37 already concluded.

findings.summary: The Status note routes security.md rule 3's range half to M5.45c criterion 5, and criterion 5 declines the range entirely -- so the obligation is dropped, not carried, and decision (b)'s coordinates are left with no consumer.
findings.detail: The added note says "The range half of security.md rule 3 that this record leaves open is carried by M5.45c's criterion 5". Criterion 5 (backlog.md:64) says the request is the WHOLE OBJECT. security.md:13 is "read-only, scoped to one key and where possible one range", and ADR-0043 decision (b) already fixed the grant as key-scoped; with a whole-object request there is no range anywhere in the design, so rule 3's range half is answered NOT POSSIBLE rather than carried. The second consequence is unrecorded: ADR-0043:86 justifies `byteStart`/`byteLen` as "union them into ONE ranged GET ... without a directory read", and under a whole-object fetch nothing reads those fields -- the directory arrives with the object. They shipped at VERSION_3 with two golden files and are now dead wire weight, and criterion 5 says a prefix mode on SegmentReader "would be its own row" without naming or opening one.
findings.failure_scenario: Two readers diverge. A security auditor tracing rule 3 follows the ADR pointer to criterion 5 expecting a range-scoped or range-limited fetch and finds the opposite, with no record of why the rule cannot be met. And the next wire-format reader asks why SubscriptionEvent carries byteStart/byteLen that no code path reads, gets no answer from the ADR that added them, and either deletes them (a VERSION_4 change) or re-derives the ranged-GET design R1 shows is unreadable. What is needed is one sentence each: rule 3's range half is DECLINED for `direct` because SegmentReader has no partial-read mode and the grant is key-scoped; and the row (or the absence of one) that would make the coordinates load-bearing.

findings.summary: M5.45d's independence claim is wrong about which modules M5.45c touches, and does not say what stops the mode-served-before-it-can-be-fetched chain if M5.45d lands first.
findings.detail: The state cell reads "M5.45c and M5.45d are INDEPENDENT: this one touches `ingest` and that one `client`". Four lines up, M5.45c's own cell now says "`plugin` is in scope for it" -- the round-2 addition contradicts the round-2 sentence describing it. More substantively, M5.45a's cell (backlog.md:62) records that ordering is forced because "a mode that is chosen before it is served drops records (ConsumerClient.decodeInto opens delivery.segment() with no fallback, and SubscriptionHub.publishRun SWALLOWS the resulting throw)", and M5.45d mints a grant and "sends no bytes" while M5.45c is what gives the consumer a way to use one.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.45d lands first on a deployment with `directEnabled` true and a signing backend (M9's, which is the whole point of the flag). FetchPolicy elects DIRECT, the hub delivers a grant with an empty segment, ConsumerClient.decodeInto:78 calls SegmentReader.open on it, SegmentReader.java:42 throws "segment is shorter than its own preamble and footer", decodeInto:91 rethrows as UncheckedIOException and the hub swallows it as a slow subscriber -- silent record loss, the exact chain M5.45a refused to create. It is unreachable in the tree today only because `directEnabled` defaults off AND neither shipping backend presigns, and the cell asserting independence says neither. One clause naming that guard makes the claim true.

findings.summary: M5.45c has re-accumulated past one commit's worth -- the test that split M5.45b -- and its new node-scope half overlaps M5.62 without citing it.
findings.detail: As of round 2 the row owns: a new `client` interface; an ADR deciding a new adapter module or a second check-io-seam exemption; `Delivery` carrying the grant with a build-site refusal; a GATE_SCOPE=full assertion; the union-into-one-request criterion; a node-level owner reaching into `plugin` (NodeSubscriptions.clientFor at plugin/src/main/java/binjava/plugin/NodeSubscriptions.java:70 builds one ConsumerClient per RunKey, so the fetcher has to be injected through that construction); and a named, budgeted per-node residency hold for 64 independent queues. That is three modules plus an ADR. M5.62 (backlog.md:83) already owns node-scoping NodeSubscriptions for the push side and says of itself "this one crosses `client` and `plugin` and changes a transport interface"; M5.45c names it only as a shape analogy ("the M5.40a/M5.62 shape") and its state cell is a bare `todo` with no relation to it.
findings.failure_scenario: The taker starts M5.45c, discovers mid-flight that the per-node hold plus the plugin wiring is a second commit, and either splits again after writing code -- which M5.45b's own cell calls "how a wire change lands half-done" -- or lands one commit spanning client, plugin and an ADR, breaking one-task-one-commit. Alternatively M5.62 lands first with a node-scoped subscriber and M5.45c's per-node fetcher owner duplicates the holder it just built, with two residency budgets for one node's segment bytes and nothing saying which is authoritative.

findings.summary: "refuses such a prefix twice" names two messages of which only the first is reachable, and `[0, objectLen)` names a bound the consumer cannot compute.
findings.detail: SegmentReader.open checks the footer magic at :71 and only reaches the run-bounds check at :90 afterwards, so a `[0, max(byteStart+byteLen))` prefix throws "segment is truncated: no footer magic" and the "run i points outside the segment" message is never produced for that input. Separately, `objectLen` exists nowhere the consumer can reach: SegmentKey (format/src/main/java/binjava/format/SegmentKey.java:17) carries `h<headerLen>` and not the object length, the event carries grant/byteStart/byteLen/segmentKey, and a node knows only ITS OWN runs -- so max(byteStart+byteLen)+FOOTER_BYTES is not objectLen either whenever the last run of the object belongs to a different node. The criterion's own gloss ("THE WHOLE OBJECT") is the implementable statement; the interval notation is not.
findings.failure_scenario: A taker writes the falsifying case for criterion 5 by asserting both refusal messages against a truncated fixture; the second assertion cannot pass and the case is weakened or deleted. Or the taker keeps the interval literally, computes objectLen from the coordinates it has, and issues a range that stops short of the footer on every segment whose last run this node does not hold -- reproducing R1's truncation on precisely the catch-up nodes the coalescing rule is about. Saying "one unranged GET of the whole object" removes both traps and is also what a counting fetcher can assert (one request, no Range header).

findings.summary: Criterion 1c cites the row where the label defect was MEASURED (M5.47) and not the open row that owns it (M5.59), and does not record that DIRECT becomes a third unpinned label site.
findings.detail: 1c is true -- publishSegment labels each push with a segment key at two `deliver` call sites (ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/SubscriptionHub.java:419 and :425) and M5.59 (backlog.md:80, `todo`) measured that threading `delta.segments().get(0).segmentKey()` through and using it at the INLINE site alone is BUILD SUCCESSFUL across the module. But M5.59 is the row that owns closing it, and its prescribed fixture is specific: a THREE-segment delta with the held segment in the MIDDLE, because reversing a two-segment order just moves the hole. M5.45d adds a third arm that carries the same label plus the grant minted from it.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.59 lands first, extends the three-segment fixture to the INLINE and PROXY arms only because those are the two its cell enumerates, and is closed. M5.45d then adds the DIRECT arm, whose grant key is unpinned in exactly the same way, and a batched delta in which this pod's segment is not first mints a grant for another pod's object: the consumer fetches a segment that does not contain its run and gets "segment <key> carries no run for <RunKey>" (ConsumerClient.java:79) with the push recorded as successful -- ADR-0032's silent data error with a working signature on the wrong object. One clause pointing 1c at M5.59 and naming DIRECT as the third arm prevents it.
